Marathon Petroleum stock rose 0.31% today to close at $388.90, extending a strong two-week rally of 7.81%. The gain reflects tightening diesel markets: diesel hit a record high as geopolitical turmoil in Ukraine and Iran has knocked offline refinery capacity in Russia and the Middle East, while U.S. refineries are running at 98% capacity with limited room to increase output. This supply crunch supports margins for refiners like Marathon, which benefit when fuel scarcity drives prices higher relative to crude oil costs.

The broader backdrop amplifies this dynamic—U.S. oil prices have climbed over 9% this week alone as military tensions between the U.S. and Iran escalate, and the EU has now formally joined sanctions against Iran that threaten to tighten global oil supply further. With diesel storage at just 104 million barrels and refineries already running near maximum, any additional disruption to offshore or refinery production would put further upward pressure on fuel prices, which is exactly the environment where refiner profits expand.
